title: Probing client emulator and variance mitigation
content:
Purpose:
This note documents a client-side emulator design and a set of controls intended to reduce measurement variance and improve repeatability for our throughput benchmarks. Focus is on: deterministic sampling strategies, backpressure handling, priming/warmup equivalence checks, and lightweight post-run diagnostics. This is a working doc: experiments + configs are recorded below.

Context and motivation:
- Our current throughput runs occasionally show 5-12% run-to-run variability on identical model/server builds. Root causes seen so far: client-side burstiness, uneven priming of KV caches, clock skew in multi-host drivers, and measurement window boundary effects.
- We need a reproducible harness for (a) comparing kernel/runtime changes, (b) validating autoscaling policies, and (c) producing repeatable perf numbers for PR/benchmarks.

High-level goals:
- Produce runs where the 95th percentile of run mean throughput across N=5 runs is within +/-3% for stable configs.
- Provide deterministic configuration hooks (seeds, request order rules) so runs can be replayed.
- Capture diagnostics automatically when variance exceeds thresholds.

Emulator architecture (client-side):
- Worker pool model: M workers per driver instance. Each worker maintains its own RNG (seeded from a per-run master seed) and a local schedule to avoid synchronized bursts.
- Request pacing: token-bucket per worker with deterministic refill schedule (driven by wall-clock + monotonic tick).
- Global coordinator: optional; used when precise phase alignment is required (e.g., priming window end). Coordinator only emits phase signals, not per-request decisions to avoid central bottleneck.
- Two emission modes:
  1) Traced deterministic mode: all event timestamps, seeds, and request indices are logged to a compressed trace file for replay.
  2) Stochastic-but-seeded mode: allows jitter but reproducible given the same master seed.

Sampling and schedule strategies (to reduce variance):
- Stratified sampling of sequence lengths: keep per-run distribution identical by sampling from a stored histogram (derived from production traces).
- Inter-request jitter model: use a low-discrepancy sequence (Sobol) to generate inter-arrival offsets where we care about even coverage; fall back to seeded PRNG otherwise.
- Client-side batching emulation: when benchmarking multi-request batching paths, use fixed-size micro-batches assembled deterministically from the worker's queue (not relying on timing-driven coalescing alone).

Priming (warmup) equivalence experiments:
- Observation: different priming strategies (single long prefix vs. many short prefixes) produce measurable differences in steady throughput and latency. Need to define equivalence class.
- Experiment plan: run 4 priming regimes:
  A) Long prefix priming: N_requests of long sequences until server reports KV-cache hit-rate plateau.
  B) Short prefix churn: many short requests that touch many KV cache slots.
  C) Mixed: alternate long/short in fixed cadence.
  D) Empty: no deliberate priming (baseline).
- Metric: time-to-steady-state (defined as 5-minute window where mean throughput variance < 1% and per-token latency stable).
- Deliverable: minimal priming recipe that yields steady-state within 2x of the best observed latency and within 5% throughput.

Repeatability controls and instrumentation:
- Master run-seed: every run has a single 64-bit hex seed placed in run metadata and in the trace header.
- Worker-local RNG state snapshots: at start and end of run, saved for replay.
- Deterministic ordering layer: when using fixed request sets, the driver must preserve insertion order to workers (no random sharding unless seeded).
- Time sync: enforce monotonic timestamps and log NTP/Chrony offsets for every driver host. If skew > 5ms, abort and report.
- Process affinity: encourage pinning of load-driver threads to CPUs; log affinity map in run metadata.

Measurement and aggregation windows:
- Priming window: adjustable, default 180s. No metrics from this window contribute to steady-state aggregates.
- Ramp window: first 60s after priming end, used for warm SLO diagnostics but not for final numbers.
- Steady-state window: contiguous window of at least 300s where throughput variance criterion holds. Aggregate metrics here.
- Boundary alignment: all drivers align steady-state window start using coordinator signal to avoid partial-window artifacts.

Noise reduction heuristics:
- Per-worker smoothing: maintain sliding median over 1s for per-worker throughput to reduce microburst noise when aggregating.
- Outlier trimming: drop top and bottom 0.5% of per-request latency before computing percentile stats for reporting (do not remove them from raw logs).
- Variance alarm: if run-to-run mean throughput stdev > 3% across N=3 preliminary runs, trigger a diagnostic capture (kernel perf, nvidia-smi sampled every 250ms, systemload trace).

Backpressure and overload behavior:
- Driver must detect server-level 429/503 and engage exponential backoff per worker. Backoff decisions are deterministic when seeded.
- When backpressure observed, mark run as contaminated unless controller approves a stress test run. Contaminated runs are archived but not used in baseline comparisons.

Config examples (representative):
- master_seed: "0x7f3ac2b1e4d5a9f0"
- workers_per_driver: "16"
- token_bucket_rate: "1200 req/s per-driver"
- token_bucket_size: "240"
- priming_strategy: "mixed"
- priming_target: "cache-hit-rate >= 92% OR 180s"
- steady_state_min_window: "300s"
- variance_threshold_pct: "3"

Logging and artifacts produced:
- run-metadata.json (driver params, seed, host map, affinity)
- trace-{seed}.ndjson.gz (per-request events with deterministic IDs)
- perf-diagnostics.zip (if variance alarm or backpressure)
- aggregated-report.csv (per-window aggregates and percentile tables)

Experiment checklist (run owner):
- [ ] verify NTP/chrony < 5ms on all hosts
- [ ] ensure driver binary built with deterministic flags (strip timestamps where possible)
- [ ] set master_seed and note it in PR/issue
- [ ] run 3 preliminary warmup-only runs, check variance alarm
- [ ] if alarm fires, run diagnostics and raise ticket with artifacts
- [ ] once stable, run N=5 final runs and archive traces with run-metadata

Diagnostics to attach to PRs comparing builds:
- aggregated-report.csv from N runs
- trace files for one representative run per build
- perf-diagnostics.zip if any anomalies observed

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Is strict determinism (no jitter) desirable for all experiments? That reduces noise but may miss real-world effects from request timing. Proposal: default to stochastic-but-seeded, with a strict-deterministic toggle for CI microbenchmarks.
- How aggressively should we trim latency outliers? Trimming hides tail events but improves signal for mean throughput comparisons. Keep raw logs always; trim only for comparison tables.
- Coordinator complexity vs. driver independence: coordinator simplifies window alignment but is an operational point-of-failure. Use coordinator only for release-grade runs; ad-hoc experiments may run independent mode.

Next steps / action items:
- [Jared] prototype Sobol-based jitter generator and add seed snapshotting hooks (due 2024-11-01).
- [Priya] implement variance alarm and perf snapshot capture in load-driver (due 2024-11-08).
- [Nora] run priming equivalence matrix against two production model configs and summarize (due 2024-11-12).

Appendix: quick replay recipe
1) locate trace-{seed}.ndjson.gz and run-metadata.json from the archived run.
2) start driver with --replay-trace path/to/trace and --preserve-worker-count.
3) use --strict-timing to reproduce exact inter-arrival times, or omit to let seeded PRNG decide micro-jitter.
4) compare output traces (MD5) and latency distributions.

Notes to self (raw):
- saw weird 11% dip when mixing long prefixes + high concurrency (maybe KV thrash) — need to tie to GPU mem bandwidth counters.
- consider lightweight per-request 'touch' to reduce cache eviction churn during priming (very experimental).

If you run anything from this doc, paste results to the INF-987 ticket and attach the run-metadata.

-- Nora
